# dsh-mcp-console
An MCP server manager for DeepSeek Harness. One page in the sidebar: add, edit, enable/disable, sign
in, import/export, and diagnose MCP servers.
## Features
- **One list, real state.** Green = connected, yellow = needs sign-in, grey = starting, red = unreac

hable, no dot = disabled. Rows sort by name or by status.
- **Live changes.** Servers live in the pr
ofile patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) as `insert` entries; every edit is written there and re-applied thr

ough the loader, so no restart is needed.
- **OAuth 2.1 (authorization code + PKCE)** for HTTP serve
rs that answer 401: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, dynamic client registration, loopback call

back, token written back as an `Authorization` header.
- **JSON import/export.** Paste a Claude/Code
x `{"mcpServers": {...}}`, a server array, or DSH patch rows; export all servers back in the same sh

ape.
- **View log.** In the row menu: one-shot `initialize` + `tools/list` for HTTP servers, or a 6-
second stdout/stderr capture for stdio servers, printed as a timestamped transcript with the OAuth m
etadata when it matters.
## Install
Add to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
and append `"dsh-mcp-console"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, then restart DSH.
The tarball bundles its only runtime dependency (`yaml`).
## Open the panel
The panel registers itself as a sidebar entry named **MCP**. If you want it elsewhere, change the `o
rder` in `lib/client.js` (`sidebar.panellist` registration).
## Notes and limits
- OAuth tokens are stored in clear text inside `cordis.patch.yml`, because the official MCP client o

nly accepts static headers. Keep that file to yourself.
- No token refresh yet. When a token expires
the row returns to "needs sign-in"; clicking the button again re-authorizes (the first round trip r

egisters a client, later ones reuse it).
- Servers are written into a marker-delimited block (`# >>>
dsh-mcp-console:begin`). Other entries in that file are left untouched, including rows written by o

ther plugins.
- Tested with DSH 0.2.1 on Windows (the desktop build does not hot-apply profile confi
g, so installs and upgrades need an app restart).
## Development
Pure ESM JavaScript, no build step.
| File | Role |
| `lib/index.js` | host half: patch block I/O, status probe, OAuth routes, import/export, diagnostic

s |
| `lib/oauth.js` | discovery, DCR, PKCE, loopback callback, token exchange |
| `lib/client.js` |

web bundle, wrapped in `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` |
| `node_modules/yaml` | vendored, shipped t
hrough `bundledDependencies` |
To hack on it, link the folder into a profile (`"dsh-mcp-console": "link:<path>"` + `bundles`) and r
on it, link the folder into a profile (`"dsh-mcp-console": "link:<path>"` + `bundles`) and restart.
